messages:
Alex: Heads-up — noticed a regression on the nightly perf dashboard for /generate (hosted). Median token latency up ~25% for long-context requests (seq > 2048), spike started 2026-11-07 03:10 UTC. Same baseline models, no deploys at the time.

Maria: Hmm. I pulled the profile for a sample request (trace_id=trc_3f9a). Flamegraph shows a big jump in time inside attention kernel selection path and then falling back to slower generic attention kernel.

Maria: snippet from profiler:
```
# top stack samples
select_kernels()  42.1%  <-- decision overhead + slow fallback
fused_multihead_attn()  12.3%
generic_attention()  31.6%  <-- dominant after fallback
kv_cache_lookup()  4.0%
```

Jordan: That's interesting — selection overhead shouldn't be 42%. We recently shipped the sequence-length smoothing change (heuristic that picks kernels based on 95th pct seq). Maybe the runtime is re-evaluating kernel choices per request too often when sequences vary. Could be an expensive path.

Sam: Also seeing larger micro-batch sizes on these traces. Batching telemetry: average_microbatch_size for /generate jumped from 6 -> 14 around the same time. That increases internal memcpy churn and KV cache churn.

Sam: Batching config on affected pool: `adaptive_batching: true, max_delay_ms: 18, max_items: 48` — the combination with the new smoothing might be causing big, infrequent batches for long tails.

Maria: I also correlated KV cache metrics: miss_rate went from 1.2% -> 8.7% for the same pool. Eviction traces show more frequent cache tombstones right before the spike window.

Eva: Actionable linking idea: we should push trace_id into the per-token metric labels (and logs) so the Console per-request breakdown view can join the token-level latency series with the trace span times. Right now we only have route + model labels which makes correlation noisy.

Alex: Agreed — adding trace_id label to token latency metric would let us draw the waterfall: batch_wait -> kernel_select -> kernel_exec -> kv_lookup -> emit_token. Want to see where the extra 25% is coming from per-token.

Jordan: Quick check I ran: for trc_3f9a the per-token breakdown from local instrument shows: batch_wait 4ms, kernel_select 6ms, kernel_exec 22ms, kv_lookup 3ms, emit 1ms. For baseline traces kernel_select was ~1.5ms and kernel_exec ~16ms. So both selection and exec were up.

Maria: I captured the kernel decision inputs for one request (seq=2300):
```
{"seq_len":2300, "pref_fused": true, "hw": "A100", "profile_hist": [1200,1800,2300,2600]}
```
It looks like because the sample histogram hit high buckets the selector tried a new kernel that doesn't have optimized fused paths for our implementation and then we fell back.

Sam: Hypothesis: interaction of adaptive batching + smoothing makes the selector see more high-seq synthetic samples and flip kernels mid-run. Fix options: 1) pin kernel selection per-model-version for a short time window, 2) reduce max_delay or cap microbatch size for long-seq routes, 3) stabilize bucket boundaries for smoothing.

Eva: For dashboarding I'll add a per-route KPI panel: median token-latency by seq-bucket, plus a trace-join panel that lets you paste trace_id and overlay span boundaries on the token timeline. I can prototype a join query like: `from tokens where trace_id = "$TRACE" | join(spans by trace_id)` — depends on adding the label.

Maria: Can we also emit kernel_choice and kernel_variant as tags on the trace spans? That way the Console timeline can color tokens by variant.

Jordan: Good idea. We'll need to plumb kernel metadata from runtime into the span creation (very small payload). Should be cheap.

Alex: Plan:
- Sam + Jordan: revert smoothing heuristic to previous behavior on staging and test impact on microbatch sizes (Sam) and kernel_select overhead (Jordan). (Sam/Jordan)
- Maria: gather 20 example traces and upload profiler dumps and kv eviction traces to the incident thread. (Maria)
- Eva: prototype trace_id label on token metrics + trace-join panel in Console staging. (Eva)
- I'll schedule a 30-min sync today 10:30 PT to review before we touch prod.

Sam: I can run a quick A/B on the affected dedicated pool. If we see drop in median token-latency and microbatch size normalizes, we can roll the change to prod with a canary.

infra-bot: Deployed config snapshot 1817770000 by Alex -> saved to /deploys/runtime-configs/1817770000.json :warning: (no prod apply yet)

Jordan: One more diagnostic we should add: emit a lightweight kernel_selection_duration metric per-request (single scalar) so automated regressions can alert before median shifts. Right now we only have token-level series which smooths over selection spikes.

Alex: +1. If we can detect kernel_select dur > 5ms for >1% requests per-minute -> auto-signal pause for smoothing and trigger a canary revert.

Maria: Uploading profiler samples now (s3://redwood-debug/runtime/profiles/1817770000/). Putting a few sample flamegraphs in the thread.

Eva: I'll mock up the Console panel and add a “trace lookup” input so SREs can drop in trace ids during incident investigations.

Alex: Thanks everyone. @Sam @Jordan flag me when you have the A/B results. I'll notify eng-sre and product if we need an emergency rollout. :thumbsup:
